summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF ~20%), diabetes, hypertension, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for acute on chronic shortness of breath with sudden onset orthopnea. Evaluation ruled out pulmonary embolism, acute aortic pathology, and myocardial infarction. Imaging showed pulmonary edema superimposed on emphysematous changes and enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. The patient was treated with IV and oral diuretics, optimized on beta-blocker therapy, and educated on fluid and sodium restriction. Acute kidney injury developed, likely due to contrast and diuresis, prompting temporary discontinuation of lisinopril and metformin. Symptoms improved, and he was discharged home with services, stable on room air, with follow-up planned for renal function and consideration of a sleep study for suspected obstructive sleep apnea.
